R398.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist (RestoredSession;java.base/*;!*) is the standard, correct API for this sink and satisfies all three contract requirements without side effects.

R399.note: Canonicalization plus startsWith containment correctly closes traversal, but the write-up also drops URLDecoder.decode() entirely (unnecessary for the fix since the char/containment checks already block traversal either way), silently narrowing the accepted cookie-value format even though it is disclosed.

R400.note: fsockopen with separate host/port args fully removes the shell sink, but swaps ICMP ping semantics for fixed-port (80/443/22) TCP checks, a materially different diagnostic result (false 'unreachable' for hosts with none of those ports open) that is only briefly flagged in the explanation.

R401.note: execFile with an argument array closes shell injection and the domain regex is permissive of legitimate FQDNs; residual: regex still allows a leading '-', so whois flag/option injection is not fully addressed, though that is a narrower issue than the reported command injection.

R402.note: exec(String[]) plus a hostname/IPv6-character regex closes the reported shell injection without restricting legitimate hosts; residual leading-hyphen flag injection into ping is a narrower, unaddressed issue.

R403.note: Deny-by-default JexlSandbox plus newInstance(false) is the correct primary control, but the sandbox carries no explicit permits for the ReportRow class that is still exposed to expressions as context variable 'row', silently breaking any filter that calls row.<method>() - not mentioned in the write-up.

R404.note: Build FAILs: imports org.owasp.html.Encode, which does not exist (OWASP Java Encoder's class is org.owasp.encoder.Encode), so the file does not compile and the endpoint is entirely broken.

R405.note: Native System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping removes the PowerShell/process sink entirely and closely reproduces the original ICMP ping count/statistics output, with no new restriction on legitimate serverName values.

R406.note: JNDI parameterized filter ({0}/{1} plus filterArgs) is the correct native-escaping API for this sink, preserving the original OR-filter semantics exactly via automatic RFC4515 escaping rather than rejecting input.

R407.note: CRLF-reject closes the inline-protocol injection but keeps the deliberately non-standard raw inline protocol (comment notes it bypasses StackExchange.Redis's RESP framing) instead of switching to length-prefixed RESP framing, which would not need to reject embedded CRLF; as implemented it also rejects any legitimate multi-line note text via an uncaught ArgumentException, disclosed but not softened.

R408.note: archive/tar-based native listing removes the shell sink and matches the text/plain/400/500 contract items, but the ctx context.Context parameter is never used in the new body, silently dropping the stated 'continues using the request context for cancellation' requirement.
